title: Introduce econ-lane-harmonizer CLI and compact quant thresholds
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new CLI tool (econ-lane-harmonizer) to generate tenant-aware batch/caching lane presets and a compact quantization threshold profile. Backwards-compatible defaults; non-breaking. Includes telemetry for lane selection and unit-econ deltas.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a lightweight CLI (tools/econ-lane-harmonizer) plus runtime config glue to produce balanced 'lanes' for batching/caching defaults and a conservative compact quantization threshold profile that reduces unit cost while preserving edge-case quality.

Motivation: customers need deterministic, automated lane suggestions that respect both latency SLOs and tenant unit economics. Existing autotuners focus on throughput; this CLI provides a deterministic prescriptor for initial defaults and a safe quant threshold fallback path.

What is included: 1) tools/econ-lane-harmonizer: a Go-based CLI that consumes sampled workload histograms (token lengths, arrival rates, cold-start frequency) and outputs a manifest of lane presets (batch_size, max_latency_ms, cache_ttl_ms, quant_profile). The CLI supports dry-run and export-as-code (YAML) modes. 2) runtime integration: a small runtime adapter that can consume the YAML presets and translate them into the ServingRuntime's lane definitions (redwood/runtime/lanes_adapter.go). 3) quant profiles: introduces "compact-q" threshold set under models/quant-profiles/compact.json with conservative per-layer fallthrough rules and a runtime-safe degrade path that prefers latency-preserving quantization for short sequences. 4) telemetry: new events (telemetry/econ_lane_choice) and unit-econ delta metrics (unit_econ.delta.percent) to evaluate suggested lanes in canary. 5) tests and docs: unit tests for the CLI, e2e smoke tests that run generated lanes in the local benchmark lab, and a new docs page (docs/cli/econ-lane-harmonizer.md) with examples.

Commits (high-level): - a1b3f2e: initial CLI scaffold and histogram parser - 9c2d0b4: lane scoring algorithm (cost-latency tradeoff) - 4f7e8ab: YAML export + runtime adapter + tests - b3c2f11: compact quant profile + quant rollback hooks - e571ad9: telemetry events and dashboards + docs

Changes (high-level file list): - tools/econ-lane-harmonizer/main.go (new) - tools/econ-lane-harmonizer/README.md (new) - redwood/runtime/lanes_adapter.go (modified) - models/quant-profiles/compact.json (new) - telemetry/events/econ_lane_choice.yaml (new) - docs/cli/econ-lane-harmonizer.md (new) - integration-tests/cli/econ_lane_smoke_test.sh (new) - pkg/config/schema.yaml (minor addition: lane_presets export) - ci/workflows/econ-lane-ci.yml (new lightweight CI for CLI)

Testing & CI: CI run targeted CLI unit tests (go test ./tools/...), staticcheck, and a lightweight integration that runs the smoke script under a local fakeruntime. Initial CI run had a lint failure (go vet) which was fixed in commit 4f7e8ab. Final CI status: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration).

Review conversation (high-level): - Arjun: "Can the lane scoring be tuned per-tenant via feature flag?" Reply: "Yes — the CLI emits a 'tuneHint' field and the runtime adapter reads tenant overrides; documented in CLI README. We added a RFC-style flag --tenant-overrides to the CLI." - Sofia: "Telemetry looks noisy, can we aggregate at 1m buckets?" Reply: "Aggregated server-side by default, added config.telemetry.bucket_seconds=60 and updated event schema." - Liam: "Quant rollback path: please ensure there's an automatic safety net on quality regression." Reply: "Added a quality-check hook that compares canary responses against reference prompts; if regression > 2% we auto-disable compact-q for that tenant."

Approvals & merge: After addressal of comments, reviewers approved (Arjun, Sofia, Liam). Merge method: squash and merge.

Post-merge actions: - Run canary on limited tenants for 48 hours (QA ticket created) - Dashboard: added econ-lane-view to Console (telemetry dashboard) - Docs: publish CLI doc page to docs site.

Migration notes: No forced migration. Customers using existing defaults are unaffected; operators can run the CLI to generate lane presets and import them via the Console or CLI.

Security & privacy: No secret material in repo. Telemetry events contain only aggregated numeric counters and hashed tenant IDs; added consent note in telemetry schema.

Performance impact: Benchmarks on benchmark-lab showed median latency change <1% and unit cost reduction ~6% for medium token workloads with compact-q applied on warm lanes.

Rollout plan: Canary (10 tenants) -> Canary expansion (100 tenants) -> Global.

Related work items: ENG-2187 (lane prescriptor), ENG-2190 (quant fallback safety harness), SUP-4321 (support request: tenant cost nudges).

Notes for releases: algorithm is heuristic-based; we should track unit_econ.delta.percent in the 2-week sprint.

Contact: Maya Chen (author) for followups.
